title: Minimum Edge Reversals So Every Node Is Reachable
summary: Given a directed graph with n nodes, where each node is labeled from 0 to n-1, and the graph forms a tree if edges are bidirectional, calculate the minimum number of edge reversals needed from each node to ensure all other nodes are reachable.
statement: Given a directed graph with n nodes, where each node is labeled from 0 to n-1, and the graph forms a tree if edges are bidirectional, calculate the minimum number of edge reversals needed from each node to ensure all other nodes are reachable. Return an array where each element represents the minimum reversals needed from the corresponding node.
constraints: Ignoring directions, edges form a tree on nodes 0 through n-1.
answer[i] is the reversals needed to make every node reachable from i.
hints: After computing one root, moving the root across one edge changes only that edge’s required direction.
Store each undirected adjacency with whether traversal needs reversal; DFS once from zero, then reroot.
answer[child]=answer[parent]+1 for an originally parent-to-child edge, otherwise -1.
All other edges keep their parent-child orientation, so this single-edge delta produces every root’s optimum.

tests.explanation: Rooting at each node gives reversal counts one, one, zero, and two.
The directed chain already points outward only from node one after one reroot adjustment.
